:::{#def-linear-code}
#### Linear code

Let the alphabet be a finite field $\ffield{q}$,
such as $\ffield{2} = \set{0, 1}$ with addition and multiplication modulo 2.
A **linear code** is a [block code](#def-block-code)
whose set of codewords $C$ is a $k$-dimensional subspace of $\ffield{q}^n$.
One way to describe it is by a **parity-check matrix**:
an $(n - k) \times n$ matrix $H$ of rank $n - k$ with
$C = \set{y \in \ffield{q}^n : H y = 0}$,
where $y$ is treated as a column vector.
A linear code with block length $n$, dimension $k$
and [minimum distance](#def-hamming-distance) $d$
is called an $\codeparams{n}{k}{d}{q}$ code.

:::
